chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a people in a village who have no one to gather with for prayer: do they pray the Dhuhr prayer on Friday in congregation? He said, 'Yes, if they do not fear [harm].'
Thus, he (peace be upon him) explicitly stated in this narration that Friday prayer is only permissible if the situation is not one of precautionary piety (taqiyyah).
As for the Qunut on Friday, if a person prays in congregation, he performs Qunut in the first rak'ah before bowing (ruku'), and in the second rak'ah after bowing.
And if he prays individually, he performs Qunut in the second rak'ah before bowing.
And that which indicates this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for Qunut timing in Friday prayer when praying in congregation versus individually?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that Friday prayer remains valid even without a full congregation provided there is no fear of persecution (*taqiyyah*), highlighting the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in varying political climates. It further specifies the distinct ritual practice of *Qunut*, distinguishing between the pre-ruku' recitation in the first rak'ah during congregational prayer and the post-ruku' recitation in the second rak'ah when praying individually, reflecting the nuanced transmission of Imami legal traditions.
